answer: Aging trust turns time into the attacker's enemy: a new identity starts with almost no privileges and earns capability only through a long, verifiable history of useful work, like a beacon that must burn steadily before anyone follows. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand clones, but each is an oasis with no water — no history, no endorsements, no earned weight — until it survives the same slow maturation as an honest agent. Through this prism, bulk creation buys only waiting: the cost is not money but months of idle, detectable clones, and any burst of fresh identities is trivially quarantined.
